title: Clark Drops Tony to 64.8, and Four Teams Are 7–4
dek: Clark's 64.6-point beatdown of Tony creates a four-way tie for first, Prithvi comes back from 30% against Stephen, and a 5–6 Clark now has better playoff odds than three of the leaders.

sections.head: The lead
body: Tony scored 64.8 this week, the lowest total of the season, and Clark beat him 129.4–64.8. The 64.6-point margin is the biggest beatdown of the year and the upset of the week: Tony was rated 117 Elo points higher. Clark leads the series 12–9.

The result is a four-way tie at 7–4: Tyler, Tony, Prithvi and Sagar. And the most dangerous team in the league might be the one behind them. Clark is 5–6 but has scored the most points (1463.4), is the unluckiest manager in the league (scored like a 6.8-win team), and the playoff model puts 7th Floor Crew at **80%**, second only to Tony's 85%.

sections.head: Comeback of the week
body: Stephen had Prithvi down to a 30% win chance at Sun 2:00pm, helped along by Ladd McConkey's 6-yd TD catch and Fernando Mendoza's 19-yd TD pass to Thomas, each worth a 28% swing, plus Ashton Jeanty's 68-yd TD catch for another 22%. Prithvi won anyway, 154.8–126.0, with the week's top score. Stephen still leads the series 6–3.

The swing was enormous in the standings. Prithvi's playoff odds rose 14 points to 74%, and Ambiance and Decor moved to No. 1 in the power rankings. Stephen, the league's luckiest manager at 6–5, fell from 24% to 9%. The replays are on the site.

sections.head: Around the league
body: Tyler beat Evan 145.6–120.1 and leads the series 14–9. Tyler is averaging 132.6 a game, close to Stephen's season record of 133.9 from 2024; Clark (133.0), Tony (131.0) and Prithvi (130.3) are all chasing the same mark.
Peyton beat Kyle 149.7–112.6 despite Travis Kelce's 8-yd TD catch swinging it 27% toward Kyle, and leads that series 11–9. Sagar beat Greg 116.6–89.9 to square their series at 11–11.

sections.head: Power shifts
body: The ratings still like Tony best at **+5.1**, the loss notwithstanding, followed by Prithvi (+3.6) and Clark (+2.6). The awkward one is Tyler: tied for first at 7–4, rated +0.5, seventh in the league. Greg sits last at −10.8, well behind a 1–10 Evan at −3.9.

sections.head: The playoff picture
body: Four spots, four weeks left. Tony is at 85% (down from 94%), Clark 80%, Tyler 76% (up 15 points) and Prithvi 74%. Sagar is a coin flip at 50%. Peyton climbed from 15% to 23%, while Kyle fell from 15% to 3%. Evan and Greg are out of it.

sections.head: Game of the Week
body: Prithvi vs Tyler, two 7–4 teams with a 58% playoff swing between them. Prithvi is projected 127.0–125.1 with a 53% chance; Joe Burrow is projected for 24.7 for Tyler and Jahmyr Gibbs for 23.4 for Prithvi. Tyler owns the series 14–5.

Clark vs Sagar is nearly as big, a 50% swing between two managers tied 11–11 all time; Sagar is a 58% favorite. Tony visits Stephen at 61%, and leads that series 7–2. Peyton gets Evan at 59%, though Evan leads their series 14–8.

groupme: Week 11 issue is up. Tony scored 64.8 and Clark beat him by 64.6, the biggest beatdown of the year. Now four teams are 7–4, and the 5–6 team has the second-best playoff odds. Prithvi came back from 30% on Stephen. Next week Prithvi and Tyler play with a 58% playoff swing on the line, and Tyler owns that series 14–5.
